text: The camera occlusion, we did the walls. and roof. we need to do the heightfields next. just realized it is going inside of the msh
resolution: Camera spring-arm now collides with terrain/ramp HEIGHTFIELDS, not just wall/roof boxes — the camera was dipping inside hills/slopes because heightfields are a separate sampled collider type absent from the rect buffer the spring-arm tested. Added framework/game/physics.zig cameraOcclusionHeightfields: a bounded march (8..64 samples) of the camera->pivot segment against heightfieldSurfaceAt, returning the distance from the pivot where terrain first rises into the line of sight (0 = clear) — catches a hill blocking the view AND the eye sitting inside a slope. world_loader.zig springArmEye now queries both the wall colliders and the heightfields and pulls the eye to the most-restrictive (min) cap, and runs even with no wall colliders (terrain-only areas). Needs a loader rebuild (rjit game play/shot). Verified loader builds clean (zig build app -Duse-v8=false), physics 15/15 + cameraOcclusion 3/3, zig fmt clean. world_loader.zig also swept another active session's in-progress buildPhysicsColliders work (compiled clean). The editor's JS spring-arm can take the same heightfield query for parity next. Commit 10f82997b.
